title.zh: 卷369 列傳一百五十六 林则徐 邓廷桢 达洪阿
title.en: Volume 369 Biographies 156: Lin Zexu, Deng Tingzhen, Da Hong A
title.raw: 卷369 列傳一百五十六 林则徐 邓廷桢 达洪阿

sentences.zh: 林則徐 ，字少穆，福建侯官人。

translations.literal: Lin Zexu, styled Shaomu, was a native of Houguan in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Zexu, whose courtesy name was Shaomu, came from Houguan in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 少警敏，有異才。

translations.literal: In youth he was alert and keen, and possessed unusual talent.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was quick-witted and showed exceptional ability.

sentences.zh: 年二十，舉鄉試。

translations.literal: At age twenty he passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he passed the provincial civil service examination.

sentences.zh: 巡撫張師誠闢佐幕。

translations.literal: The governor Zhang Shicheng invited him to serve on his staff.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Zhang Shicheng recruited him as a staff adviser.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十六年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Jiaqing he became a jinshi, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In 1811 he passed the metropolitan examination, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and was appointed a compiler.

sentences.zh: 歷典江西、雲南鄉試，分校會試。

translations.literal: He successively presided over the provincial examinations in Jiangxi and Yunnan and served as an associate examiner for the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as chief examiner for the provincial examinations in Jiangxi and Yunnan and as an associate examiner for the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 遷御史，疏論福建閩安副將張寶以海盜投誠，宜示裁抑，以防驕蹇，被嘉納。

translations.literal: He was transferred to censor and memorialized that Fujian's Min'an deputy commander Zhang Bao, having surrendered as a pirate, should be shown restraint and curbed to guard against arrogance and insolence; this was praised and accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to censor, he memorialized that Deputy Commander Zhang Bao of Min'an in Fujian, who had surrendered after a career as a pirate, ought to be kept in check lest he grow arrogant and overbearing; the throne approved his advice.

sentences.zh: 未幾，出為杭嘉湖道，修海塘，興水利。

translations.literal: Before long he went out as intendant of the Hang-Jia-Hu Circuit, repaired sea dikes, and promoted water conservancy.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was posted as intendant of the Hangzhou-Jiaxing-Huzhou circuit, where he repaired sea dikes and advanced hydraulic works.

sentences.zh: 道光元年，聞父病，引疾歸。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daoguang, hearing that his father was ill, he cited illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: In 1821, on hearing that his father was ill, he asked leave on grounds of illness and went home.

sentences.zh: 二年，起授淮海道，未之任，署浙江鹽運使。

translations.literal: In the second year he was recalled and appointed intendant of the Huai-Hai Circuit, but before taking up the post he served as acting salt controller of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was recalled and appointed intendant of the Huai-Hai circuit, though before assuming that post he acted as Zhejiang salt controller.

sentences.zh: 遷江蘇按察使，治獄嚴明。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Jiangsu judicial commissioner and administered cases with strict clarity.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Jiangsu judicial commissioner and gained a reputation for strict, impartial adjudication.

sentences.zh: 四年，大水，署布政使，治賑。

translations.literal: In the fourth year there was a great flood; he acted as provincial treasurer and managed relief.
translations.idiomatic: In 1824, when severe flooding struck, he served as acting provincial treasurer and directed famine relief.

sentences.zh: 尋丁母憂，命赴南河修高家堰堤工，事竣回籍。

translations.literal: Soon after he entered mourning for his mother; he was ordered to the Southern Rivers to repair the Gaojia Embankment works, and when the work was finished he returned to his native place.
translations.idiomatic: He soon entered mourning for his mother, but was ordered to the Southern Rivers to repair the Gaojia Embankment; when the project was complete he returned home.

sentences.zh: 六年，命署兩淮鹽政，以未終制辭，服闋，補陝西按察使。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was ordered to act as Lianghuai salt controller, but declined because mourning was not yet complete; after mourning ended he was appointed Shaanxi judicial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In 1826 he was ordered to act as Lianghuai salt controller but declined while still in mourning; when mourning ended he was appointed Shaanxi judicial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 遷江寧布政使，父憂歸。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Jiangning provincial treasurer, then returned home on his father's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Jiangning provincial treasurer, then went home to observe mourning for his father.

sentences.zh: 十年，補湖北布政使，調河南，又調江寧。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he filled the post of Hubei provincial treasurer, was transferred to Henan, and again to Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: In 1830 he was appointed Hubei provincial treasurer, then transferred to Henan and again to Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 十一年，擢河東河道總督。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was promoted to governor-general of the Eastern Henan River Conservancy.
translations.idiomatic: In 1831 he was promoted to governor-general in charge of the Eastern Henan river works.

sentences.zh: 疏陳稭料為河工第一弊藪，親赴各廳察驗；

translations.literal: He memorialized that straw materials were the foremost abuse in river works and personally went to each office to inspect and verify;
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that straw supplies were the worst abuse in river engineering and personally inspected every office;

sentences.zh: 又言碎石實足為埽工之輔，應隨宜施用。

translations.literal: he also said that broken stone could truly assist revetment work and should be applied as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: he also argued that crushed stone could effectively supplement revetment works and ought to be used wherever appropriate.

sentences.zh: 十二年，調江蘇巡撫。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was transferred to Jiangsu governor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1832 he was transferred to governor of Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 吳中洊飢，奏免逋賦，籌撫卹。

translations.literal: Wu suffered repeated famine; he memorialized to remit arrears of tax and organized relief and consolation.
translations.idiomatic: When famine struck the lower Yangzi region again, he memorialized for remission of tax arrears and organized relief.

sentences.zh: 前在籓司任，議定賑務章程，行之有效，至是仍其法，宿弊一清。

translations.literal: Earlier, while serving as provincial treasurer, he had drawn up regulations for relief work that proved effective; now he applied the same methods and long-standing abuses were entirely cleared.
translations.idiomatic: While provincial treasurer he had drafted relief regulations that had worked well; he now applied them again and swept away entrenched abuses.

sentences.zh: 賑竣，乃籌積穀備荒。

translations.literal: When relief was finished, he then planned grain reserves against famine.
translations.idiomatic: After relief was complete, he set about building grain reserves against future dearth.

sentences.zh: 清釐交代，盡結京控諸獄。

translations.literal: He cleared up handovers of accounts and settled all cases appealed to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He straightened out fiscal handovers and cleared every case that had been appealed to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 考覈屬吏，疏言：「察吏莫先於自察，必將各屬大小政務，逐一求盡於心，然後能以驗群吏之盡心與否。

translations.literal: Examining subordinate officials, he memorialized: "In inspecting officials nothing comes before self-inspection; one must master in mind every great and small affair of government under one's jurisdiction, and only then can one test whether the host of officials are doing their utmost."
translations.idiomatic: Reviewing his subordinates, he memorialized: "The first step in judging officials is to judge oneself: only when a superior has mastered every major and minor affair under his charge can he tell whether his subordinates are doing their duty."

sentences.zh: 如大吏之心先未貫徹，何從察其情偽？

translations.literal: If the mind of the high official is not first thorough throughout, how can one discern truth from falsehood?
translations.idiomatic: If the superior's own understanding is incomplete, how can he discern sincerity from pretense?

sentences.zh: 臣惟持此不敢不盡之心，事事與僚屬求實際。

translations.literal: Your servant holds only this heart that dares not fail in thoroughness, and in every matter seeks practical results with colleagues and subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant holds only to this principle of thoroughness and seeks practical results in every matter together with his colleagues.

sentences.zh: 」詔嘉之，勉以力行。

translations.literal: An edict praised this and exhorted him to carry it out vigorously.
translations.idiomatic: The throne praised the memorial and urged him to put it into practice.

sentences.zh: 先是總督陶澍奏濬三江，則徐方為臬司，綜理其事，旋以憂去。

translations.literal: Earlier Governor-General Tao Shu had memorialized to dredge the Three Rivers; Lin was then judicial commissioner and oversaw the matter, but soon left on mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Governor-General Tao Shu had proposed dredging the Three Rivers, Lin as provincial treasurer had overseen the work, but he soon left office to observe mourning.

sentences.zh: 至是黃浦、吳淞工已竣，則徐力任未竟者，劉河工最要，撥帑十六萬五千有奇，白茆次要，官紳集捐十一萬兩，同時開濬，以工代賑。

translations.literal: By then the Huangpu and Wusong works were finished; Lin took on what remained, the Liu River project being most important, with 165,000-odd taels from the treasury; the Baimao project was secondary, with officials and gentry raising 110,000 taels in donations; dredging began at the same time, relief being given through labor.
translations.idiomatic: By then the Huangpu and Wusong projects were complete; Lin took charge of what remained. The Liu River was the priority, funded with more than 165,000 taels from the treasury; the Baimao works were secondary, with officials and gentry contributing 110,000 taels. Both were dredged at once, with relief provided through public works.

sentences.zh: 兩河舊皆通海，易淤，且鑿河工鉅，改為清水長河，與黃埔、吳淞交匯通流。

translations.literal: Both rivers formerly all reached the sea, silted easily, and dredging was costly; they were changed into long clear-water channels joining and flowing with Huangpu and Wusong.
translations.idiomatic: Both rivers had formerly opened to the sea, silted easily, and cost a fortune to dredge; they were converted into long freshwater channels that joined the Huangpu and Wusong.

sentences.zh: 各於近海修閘建壩，潮汐泥沙不能壅入，內河漲，則由壩洩出歸海。

translations.literal: At each place near the sea sluices and dams were built so tidal mud and sand could not choke in; when inner rivers rose, water was released through the dams back to the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Sluices and dams were built near the coast so tidal silt could not choke the channels; when inland waters rose, the surplus was discharged through the dams to the sea.

sentences.zh: 复就原河逢灣取直​​，節省工費三萬餘兩，用濬附近劉河之七浦河，及附近白茆之徐六涇、東西護塘諸河。

translations.literal: He also straightened the original river where it bent, saving more than 30,000 taels in labor costs, and used the savings to dredge the Qipu River near the Liu River, and the Xuliu Jing and East and West Hutang rivers near Baimao.
translations.idiomatic: He also cut straight channels where the old course wound, saving more than 30,000 taels, and applied the savings to dredge the Qipu River near the Liu River and the Xuliu Jing and East and West Hutang rivers near Baimao.

sentences.zh: 又濬丹徒、丹陽運河，寶帶橋泖淀諸工，以次興舉，為吳中數十年之利。

translations.literal: He further dredged the Dantu and Danyang canals and works at Baodai Bridge and the Mao lakes, undertaking them in sequence, to the benefit of Wu for decades.
translations.idiomatic: He also dredged the canals at Dantu and Danyang and works at Baodai Bridge and the Mao lakes in turn, bringing decades of benefit to the lower Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 兩署兩江總督。

translations.literal: He twice acted as governor-general of the Two Jiangs.
translations.idiomatic: He twice served as acting governor-general of the Two Jiangs.

sentences.zh: 十七年，擢湖廣總督。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was promoted to governor-general of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: In 1837 he was promoted to governor-general of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 荊、襄歲罹水災，大修堤工，其患遂弭。

translations.literal: Jing and Xiang suffered flood disasters year after year; he undertook major dike works and the affliction was then stilled.
translations.idiomatic: The Jing and Xiang regions had suffered annual floods; he launched major dike repairs and the flooding ceased.

sentences.zh: 整頓鹽課，以減價敵私無成效，專嚴緝私之禁，銷數大增。

translations.literal: He put the salt tax in order; lowering prices to compete with smuggling had no effect, so he devoted himself solely to strict prohibition of smuggling, and sales increased greatly.
translations.idiomatic: He reformed the salt monopoly: cutting prices to undercut smugglers had failed, so he tightened enforcement against illicit trade, and legal sales rose sharply.

sentences.zh: 湖南鎮筸兵悍，數肇釁，巡閱撫馭，密薦總兵楊芳，擢為提督，移駐辰州，慎固苗疆屯防。

translations.literal: The Zhenqian troops of Hunan were fierce and repeatedly provoked trouble; he toured to pacify and control them, secretly recommended Brigadier Yang Fang, promoted him to provincial commander, moved his headquarters to Chenzhou, and carefully secured Miao frontier garrison colonies.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhenqian garrison in Hunan was unruly and prone to disturbances; Lin toured the region to calm the troops, secretly recommended Brigadier Yang Fang for promotion to provincial commander, posted him at Chenzhou, and strengthened defenses along the Miao frontier.

sentences.zh: 十八年，鴻臚寺卿黃爵滋請禁鴉片煙，下中外大臣議。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year Grand Secretary of the Court of State Ceremonial Huang Juesi requested prohibition of opium, and the matter was referred for discussion to Chinese and foreign ministers.
translations.idiomatic: In 1838 Huang Juesi of the Court of State Ceremonial memorialized for a ban on opium, and the court ordered discussion among officials at home and abroad.

sentences.zh: 則徐請用重典，言：「此禍不除，十年之後，不惟無可籌之餉，且無可用之兵。

translations.literal: Lin requested severe penalties, saying: "If this scourge is not removed, within ten years there will be not only no revenue to raise but no troops fit for use."
translations.idiomatic: Lin urged severe penalties, writing: "Unless this scourge is eradicated, within ten years the state will lack not only funds for the army but soldiers fit to fight."

sentences.zh: 」宣宗深韙之，命入覲，召對十九次。

translations.literal: The Xuanzong Emperor deeply approved this, ordered him to come to audience, and summoned him for private consultation nineteen times.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Daoguang strongly agreed and summoned him to court, consulting him privately nineteen times.

sentences.zh: 授欽差大臣，赴廣東查辦，十九年春，至。

translations.literal: He was appointed Imperial Commissioner and sent to Guangdong to investigate and handle the matter; in the spring of the nineteenth year he arrived.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Imperial Commissioner to investigate in Guangdong and arrived there in the spring of 1839.

sentences.zh: 總督鄧廷楨已嚴申禁令，捕拏煙犯，洋商查頓先避回國。

translations.literal: Governor-General Deng Tingzhen had already strictly proclaimed the ban, arrested opium offenders, and the foreign merchant Dent had fled home first.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Deng Tingzhen had already enforced the ban strictly and arrested opium offenders; the merchant Dent had fled home ahead of him.

sentences.zh: 則徐知水師提督關天培忠勇可用，令整兵嚴備。

translations.literal: Lin knew that naval commander Guan Tianpei was loyal and brave and could be used, and ordered troops drilled and placed on strict alert.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing that Admiral Guan Tianpei was loyal and capable, Lin ordered the forces drilled and kept on full alert.

sentences.zh: 檄諭英國領事義律查繳煙土，驅逐躉船，呈出煙土二萬餘箱，親蒞虎門驗收，焚於海濱，四十餘日始盡。

translations.literal: He issued a proclamation to British consul Elliot to investigate and surrender opium and expel receiving ships; more than 20,000 chests were produced; he personally went to Humen to inspect receipt and burned them on the seashore; it took more than forty days to finish.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered British consul Charles Elliot to surrender opium and expel the receiving ships at Lintin. More than 20,000 chests were turned over; Lin personally supervised their receipt at Humen and burned them on the shore, a process that took more than forty days.

sentences.zh: 請定洋商夾帶鴉片罪名，依化外有犯之例，人即正法，貨物入官，責具甘結。

translations.literal: He requested fixing the crime of foreign merchants smuggling opium: following the precedent for offenders beyond the pale, the person was immediately executed according to law and goods confiscated to the state, and they were required to furnish a written bond.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that the penalty for foreign merchants carrying opium be fixed: under the law for aliens who commit capital crimes, offenders were to be executed and goods confiscated, and merchants were required to sign bonds of good conduct.

sentences.zh: 他國皆聽命，獨義律枝梧未從。

translations.literal: Other countries all obeyed; only Elliot resisted and would not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Other nations complied, but Elliot alone held out.

sentences.zh: 於是閱視沿海砲台，以虎門為第一門戶，橫檔山、武山為第二門戶，大小虎山為第三門戶。

translations.literal: He then inspected coastal batteries: Humen as the first gateway, Hengdang Hill and Wushan as the second gateway, and Great and Little Tiger Hills as the third gateway.
translations.idiomatic: He then inspected the coastal batteries, treating Humen as the first line of defense, Hengdang Hill and Wushan as the second, and Great and Little Tiger Hills as the third.

sentences.zh: 海道至橫檔分為二支，右多暗沙，左經武山前，水深，洋船由之出入。

translations.literal: The sea route at Hengdang divided into two branches: the right had many hidden shoals; the left passed before Wushan, was deep, and foreign ships entered and left by it.
translations.idiomatic: At Hengdang the channel split: the right branch was shoal-ridden, while the left, passing Wushan, was deep and served as the route foreign ships used.

sentences.zh: 關天培創議於此設木排鐵練二重，又增築虎門之河角砲台，英國商船後至者不敢入。

translations.literal: Guan Tianpei proposed setting up double rows of wooden stakes and iron chains here, and also building additional batteries at the river corner of Humen; later-arriving British merchant ships did not dare enter.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Tianpei proposed laying double rows of wooden stakes linked by iron chains and building new batteries at the Humen bend; British merchantmen that arrived later did not dare enter.

sentences.zh: 義律請令赴澳門載貨，冀囤煙私販，嚴斥拒之，潛泊尖沙嘴外洋。

translations.literal: Elliot requested permission to go to Macao to load cargo, hoping to hoard opium for secret sale; Lin sternly refused and he secretly anchored off the outer sea at Chuenpi.
translations.idiomatic: Elliot asked to load cargo at Macao, hoping to hoard opium for smuggling; Lin refused sharply, and Elliot anchored secretly off Chuenpi.

sentences.zh: 會有英人毆斃華民，抗不交犯，遂斷其食物，撤買辦、工人以困之。

translations.literal: It happened that a Briton beat a Chinese to death and resisted surrendering the offender; food was then cut off and compradors and laborers withdrawn to press them.
translations.idiomatic: When a Briton beat a Chinese man to death and refused to surrender the culprit, Lin cut off their supplies and withdrew compradors and workers to pressure them.

sentences.zh: 七月，義律藉索食為名，以貨船載兵犯九龍山砲台，參將賴恩爵擊走之。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Elliot, under the pretext of seeking food, used cargo ships to carry troops against the Kowloon Hill battery; Assistant Commander Lai Enjue drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: In July, Elliot, claiming he needed provisions, sent armed men in cargo ships against the Kowloon battery; Assistant Commander Lai Enjue repulsed them.

sentences.zh: 疏聞，帝喜悅，報曰：「既有此舉，不可再示柔弱。

translations.literal: When the memorial was reported, the Emperor was pleased and replied: "Since this action has been taken, weakness must not be shown again."
translations.idiomatic: When Lin reported the victory, the emperor was pleased and replied: "Now that you have acted thus, you must not show weakness again."

sentences.zh: 不患卿等孟浪，但戒卿等畏葸。

translations.literal: I do not fear that you are rash, but warn you against timidity.
translations.idiomatic: I do not worry that you are too bold, only that you grow timid.

sentences.zh: 」御史步際桐言出結徒虛文，則徐以彼國重然諾，不肯出結，愈不能不向索取，持之益堅。

translations.literal: Censor Bu Jitong said that requiring bonds was empty form; Lin held that that country values promises and, refusing to give a bond, made it all the more necessary to demand one, and he held firm all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Bu Jitong argued that bonds were mere formalities, but Lin replied that the British prized their word yet refused to sign—making the demand all the more necessary—and held his ground.

sentences.zh: 尋義律浼澳門洋酋轉圜，原令載煙之船回國，貨船聽官查驗。

translations.literal: Soon Elliot asked the foreign chief at Macao to mediate; the original order was that ships that had carried opium return home, and cargo ships were to submit to official inspection.
translations.idiomatic: Elliot soon asked the Portuguese authorities at Macao to mediate: opium ships were to leave, while cargo vessels would be inspected by officials.

sentences.zh: 九月，商船已具結進口，義律遣兵船阻之，開砲來攻，關天培率游擊麥廷章奮擊敗之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month merchant ships had already given bonds and entered port; Elliot sent warships to block them, opened fire to attack, and Guan Tianpei led Lieutenant Commander Mai Tingzhang in fierce fighting and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: In September, merchant ships that had signed bonds were entering port when Elliot sent warships to block them and opened fire; Guan Tianpei and Lieutenant Commander Mai Tingzhang drove them off.

sentences.zh: 十月，又犯虎門官湧，官軍分五路進攻，六戰皆捷。

translations.literal: In the tenth month they again attacked Guanyong at Humen; government troops advanced in five columns and won victory in six engagements.
translations.idiomatic: In October the British attacked Guanyong near Humen again; imperial forces advanced in five columns and won six successive engagements.

sentences.zh: 詔停止貿易，宣示罪狀，飭福建、浙江、江蘇嚴防海口。

translations.literal: An edict halted trade, proclaimed their crimes, and ordered Fujian, Zhejiang, and Jiangsu to guard the sea mouths strictly.
translations.idiomatic: The court halted trade, published the British crimes, and ordered Fujian, Zhejiang, and Jiangsu to guard their coasts strictly.

sentences.zh: 先已授則徐兩江總督，至是調補兩廣。

translations.literal: Lin had already been appointed governor-general of the Two Jiangs; now he was transferred to fill the Two Guangs.
translations.idiomatic: Lin had already been appointed governor-general of the Two Jiangs; he was now transferred to the Two Guangs.

sentences.zh: 府尹曾望顏請罷各國通商，禁漁船出洋。

translations.literal: Prefect Zeng Wangyan requested ending trade with all countries and forbidding fishing boats to go to sea.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Zeng Wangyan proposed ending trade with all nations and banning fishing boats from going to sea.

sentences.zh: 則徐疏言：「自斷英國貿易，他國喜，此盈彼絀，正可以夷制夷。

translations.literal: Lin memorialized: "Since trade with Britain was cut off, other countries are pleased; where one gains the other loses—this is just the way to use barbarians to control barbarians."
translations.idiomatic: Lin replied in a memorial: "Since we cut off British trade, other countries are pleased at Britain's loss—this is precisely how to play foreigners against one another."

sentences.zh: 如概與之絕，轉恐聯爲一氣。

translations.literal: If one cuts off relations with all alike, one may instead fear they will unite as one force.
translations.idiomatic: If we break with everyone at once, they may unite against us.

sentences.zh: 粵民以海為生，概禁出洋，其勢不可終日。

translations.literal: Cantonese live by the sea; to forbid all going to sea could not last a single day.
translations.idiomatic: Cantonese depend on the sea for their livelihood; a total ban on going offshore could not be sustained.

sentences.zh: 」時英船寄椗外洋，以利誘奸民接濟銷菸。

translations.literal: At that time British ships anchored in the outer sea and used profit to entice traitors to supply them and sell opium.
translations.idiomatic: British ships then lay at anchor offshore, bribing local collaborators to supply them and move opium.

sentences.zh: 二十年春，令關天培密裝砲械，僱漁船疍戶出洋設伏，候夜順風縱火，焚毀附夷匪船，接濟始斷。

translations.literal: In the spring of the twentieth year he ordered Guan Tianpei secretly to equip cannon, hire fishing boats and Tanka boat people to go to sea and set ambushes, wait for night and a favorable wind to set fire, burn the traitor boats attached to the foreigners, and only then was supply cut off.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 1840 he had Guan Tianpei secretly arm fishing boats and Tanka crews for night raids; when the wind served they set fire to boats aiding the British, and the supply line was finally broken.

sentences.zh: 五月，再焚夷船於磨刀洋。

translations.literal: In the fifth month they again burned foreign ships at Modaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In May they burned more British ships at Modaoyang.

sentences.zh: 諜知新來敵船揚帆北鄉，疏請沿海各省戒嚴。

translations.literal: Spies learned that newly arrived enemy ships had set sail northward; he memorialized requesting all coastal provinces to be placed on alert.
translations.idiomatic: Intelligence reported that newly arrived enemy ships were sailing north; he memorialized for coastal provinces to go on alert.

sentences.zh: 又言夷情詭譎，若迳赴天津求通貿易，請優示懷柔，依嘉慶年間成例，將遞詞人由內地送粵。

translations.literal: He also said the foreigners were treacherous; if they went straight to Tianjin seeking trade, he asked that kindness be shown generously and, following the precedent of the Jiaqing years, the petitioners be escorted overland to Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He also warned that if the British sailed to Tianjin to demand trade, the court should treat them leniently and, following Jiaqing precedent, escort their envoys overland back to Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 六月，英船至廈門，為閩浙總督鄧廷楨所拒。

translations.literal: In the sixth month British ships reached Xiamen and were repelled by Fujian-Zhejiang Governor-General Deng Tingzhen.
translations.idiomatic: In June the British reached Xiamen and were turned back by Governor-General Deng Tingzhen of Fujian and Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 其犯浙者陷定海，掠寧波。

translations.literal: Those that invaded Zhejiang took Dinghai and plundered Ningbo.
translations.idiomatic: Those that struck Zhejiang captured Dinghai and raided Ningbo.

sentences.zh: 則徐上疏自請治罪，密陳兵事不可中止，略曰：「英夷所憾在粵而滋擾於浙，雖變動出於意外，其窮蹙實在意中。

translations.literal: Lin memorialized asking punishment for himself and secretly stated that military operations must not cease, saying in summary: "The British grievance lies in Guangdong yet they spread disturbance in Zhejiang; though the change was unexpected, their distress was really within expectation."
translations.idiomatic: Lin memorialized asking to be punished and privately urged that the war must continue, writing in part: "The British resent what happened in Guangdong yet are raiding Zhejiang; though the turn of events was unexpected, their desperation was entirely foreseeable."

sentences.zh: 惟其虛憍性成，愈窮蹙時，愈欲顯其桀驁，試其恫喝，甚且別生秘計，冀售其奸；

translations.literal: Only their nature is formed of empty arrogance; the more distressed they are, the more they wish to display defiance, test intimidation, and even devise secret schemes hoping to sell their treachery;
translations.idiomatic: They are by nature arrogant; the more cornered they are, the more they try to show defiance, test threats, and even hatch secret schemes;

sentences.zh: 一切不得行，仍必帖耳俯伏。

translations.literal: when none of this succeeds, they must still submit with ears lowered.
translations.idiomatic: when none of this succeeds, they will still submit in the end.

sentences.zh: 第恐議者以為內地船砲非外夷之敵，與其曠日持久，不如設法羈縻。

translations.literal: I only fear that deliberators will think inland ships and cannon cannot match the foreigners, and that rather than prolong the days, it is better to devise means of appeasement.
translations.idiomatic: I fear only that some will say our ships and guns cannot match theirs and that appeasement is better than a long war.

sentences.zh: 抑知夷情無厭，得步進步，威不能克，患無已時。

translations.literal: Yet know that barbarian disposition is insatiable; give an inch and they take a mile; if might cannot overcome them, calamity will have no end.
translations.idiomatic: Yet foreigners are never satisfied: concede once and they demand more; if force cannot prevail, trouble will never end.

sentences.zh: 他國紛紛效尤，不可不慮。

translations.literal: Other countries will one after another follow suit—this cannot be left unconsidered.
translations.idiomatic: Other nations may follow their example—this must not be ignored.

sentences.zh: 」因請戴罪赴浙，隨營自效。

translations.literal: He therefore asked to go to Zhejiang bearing guilt and serve in the camps to redeem himself.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to go to Zhejiang at his own risk and serve with the army there.

sentences.zh: 七月，義律至天津，投書總督琦善，言廣東燒煙之釁，起自則徐及鄧廷楨二人，索價不與，又遭詬逐，故越境呈訴。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Elliot reached Tianjin and sent a letter to Governor Qishan, saying the provocation of burning opium in Guangdong arose from Lin and Deng Tingzhen, that compensation was demanded but not given, and that they were abused and driven away, hence the appeal across borders.
translations.idiomatic: In July Elliot reached Tianjin and wrote to Governor Qishan, blaming Lin and Deng Tingzhen for the destruction of opium at Guangdong, claiming he had been denied compensation and insulted and driven off, and appealing over their heads.

sentences.zh: 琦善據以上聞，上意始動。

translations.literal: Qishan reported this upward and the emperor's mind began to waver.
translations.idiomatic: Qishan reported this to the throne, and the emperor began to change his mind.

sentences.zh: 時英船在粵窺伺，复連敗之蓮花峰下及龍穴洲。

translations.literal: At the time British ships were watching in Guangdong; they were again defeated in succession below Lianhua Peak and at Longxue Isle.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile British ships off Guangdong were defeated again below Lianhua Peak and at Longxue Isle.

sentences.zh: 捷書未上，九月，詔曰：「鴉片流毒內地，特遣林則徐會同鄧廷楨查辦，原期肅清內地，斷絕來源，隨地隨時，妥為辦理。

translations.literal: Before the victory reports arrived, in the ninth month an edict said: "Opium flows poison into the interior; Lin Zexu was specially sent together with Deng Tingzhen to investigate and handle it, originally expecting to purge the interior and cut off the source, handling matters properly in each place and time."
translations.idiomatic: Before news of these victories reached Beijing, in September an edict declared: "Opium poisons the empire; Lin Zexu was specially dispatched with Deng Tingzhen to eradicate it at home and cut off the source, handling affairs properly as circumstances required."

sentences.zh: 乃自查辦以來，內而奸民犯法不能淨盡，外而興販來源並未斷絕，沿海各省紛紛徵調，糜餉勞師，皆林則徐等辦理不善之所致。

translations.literal: Yet since the investigation began, within, law-breaking traitors could not be entirely eliminated; without, the source of the traffic was not cut off; coastal provinces were repeatedly mobilized, funds wasted and troops wearied—all caused by the poor handling of Lin Zexu and others.
translations.idiomatic: Yet since the campaign began, offenders at home have not been eliminated, the opium trade abroad has not been stopped, and coastal provinces have been mobilized at great cost—all because Lin Zexu and his colleagues handled matters badly.

sentences.zh: 」下則徐等嚴議，飭即來京，以琦善代之。

translations.literal: Lin and others were referred for severe deliberation and ordered to come immediately to the capital; Qishan was appointed in their place.
translations.idiomatic: Lin and his colleagues were ordered to Beijing for investigation and replaced by Qishan.

sentences.zh: 尋議革職，命仍回廣東備查問差委。

translations.literal: Soon it was decided to dismiss them from office and they were ordered still to return to Guangdong to await inquiry and assignment.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon dismissed from office and ordered back to Guangdong pending further inquiry.

sentences.zh: 琦善至，義律要求賠償煙價，廈門、福州開埠通商，上怒，復命備戰。

translations.literal: When Qishan arrived, Elliot demanded compensation for the opium and opening of Xiamen and Fuzhou for trade; the emperor was angry and again ordered preparations for war.
translations.idiomatic: When Qishan arrived, Elliot demanded compensation for the destroyed opium and the opening of Xiamen and Fuzhou to trade; the emperor was furious and ordered war preparations resumed.

sentences.zh: 二十一年春，予則徐四品卿銜，赴浙江鎮海協防。

translations.literal: In the spring of the twenty-first year Lin was given the fourth-rank courtier title and sent to Zhejiang Zhenhai to assist in defense.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 1841 Lin was given a fourth-rank courtier title and sent to help defend Zhenhai in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 時琦善雖以擅與香港逮治，和戰仍無定局。

translations.literal: At the time Qishan, though arrested for unauthorized cession of Hong Kong, still left peace and war undecided.
translations.idiomatic: Although Qishan had been arrested for ceding Hong Kong without authorization, peace and war remained unsettled.

sentences.zh: 五月，詔斥則徐在粵不能德威並用，褫卿銜，遣戍伊犁。

translations.literal: In the fifth month an edict rebuked Lin for failing to use both kindness and might in Guangdong, stripped his courtier title, and sent him into exile at Yili.
translations.idiomatic: In May an edict blamed Lin for failing to combine persuasion with force in Guangdong, stripped his courtier title, and exiled him to Yili.

sentences.zh: 會河決開封，中途奉命襄辦塞決，二十二年，工竣，仍赴戍，而浙江、江南師屢敗。

translations.literal: It happened that the river broke at Kaifeng; en route he was ordered to assist in blocking the breach; in the twenty-second year the work was finished and he still went to exile, while armies in Zhejiang and Jiangnan were repeatedly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yellow River burst its banks at Kaifeng, he was ordered en route to help repair the breach; in 1842, after the work was done, he continued to exile while imperial forces in Zhejiang and Jiangnan suffered repeated defeats.

sentences.zh: 是年秋，和議遂成。

translations.literal: That autumn peace was concluded.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn peace was concluded.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，新疆興治屯田，將軍布彥泰請以則徐綜其事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year garrison farming was promoted in Xinjiang; General Buyantai requested that Lin oversee the matter.
translations.idiomatic: In 1844, when garrison colonization was promoted in Xinjiang, General Buyantai asked that Lin oversee the project.

sentences.zh: 週曆南八城，濬水源，闢溝渠，墾田三萬七千餘頃，請給回民耕種，改屯兵為操防，如議行。

translations.literal: He toured the eight southern cities, dredged water sources, opened canals and ditches, and reclaimed more than 37,000 qing of fields; he requested that they be given to Hui people to cultivate and that garrison troops be changed to drill defense; this was carried out as proposed.
translations.idiomatic: He toured the eight southern cities, opened water sources and canals, and reclaimed more than 37,000 qing of land, which he proposed assigning to Hui farmers while converting garrison troops to defense duties; the plan was adopted.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，召還，以四五品京堂候補。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he was recalled and made a capital official of the fourth or fifth rank awaiting appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In 1845 he was recalled to serve as a capital official of the fourth or fifth rank awaiting appointment.

sentences.zh: 尋署陝甘總督。

translations.literal: Soon he acted as governor-general of Shaanxi-Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: He soon served as acting governor-general of Shaanxi and Gansu.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，授陝西巡撫，留甘肅，偕布彥泰治叛番，擒其酋。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was appointed Shaanxi governor, remained in Gansu, and together with Buyantai pacified rebellious tribes and captured their chief.
translations.idiomatic: In 1846 he was appointed governor of Shaanxi but remained in Gansu, where with Buyantai he suppressed rebellious tribes and captured their leader.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，授雲貴總督。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he was appointed governor-general of Yunnan-Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 1847 he was appointed governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 雲南漢、回互鬥焚殺，歷十數年。

translations.literal: In Yunnan Han and Hui had fought and burned and killed one another for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: In Yunnan, Han and Hui communities had been fighting, burning, and killing one another for more than a decade.

sentences.zh: 會保山回民控於京，漢民奪犯，毀官署，拆瀾滄江橋以拒，鎮道不能制。

translations.literal: Meanwhile, when Baoshan Hui had appealed to the capital, Han people seized the prisoners, destroyed government offices, and tore down the Lancang River bridge to resist; the prefectural and circuit officials could not control them.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile at Baoshan, Hui Muslims had petitioned Beijing; Han villagers then seized the prisoners, wrecked government offices, and demolished the Lancang River bridge to block the authorities, and local military and civil officials could not bring the situation under control.

sentences.zh: 則徐主止分良莠，不分漢、回。

translations.literal: Zexu held that one should only distinguish good from evil, not Han from Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Zexu maintained that officials should distinguish only the righteous from the wicked, not Han from Hui.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，親督師往剿，途中聞彌渡客回滋亂，移兵破其巢，殲匪數百。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he personally commanded troops to campaign against them; en route he heard that guest Hui at Midu were causing renewed disorder, shifted his army to destroy their lair, and killed several hundred bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In 1848 he personally led an expedition against them; on the march he learned that outsider Hui at Midu had risen again, diverted his forces to destroy their stronghold, and killed several hundred rebels.

sentences.zh: 保山民聞風股栗，縛犯迎師，誅其首要，散其脅從，召漢、回父老諭以恩信。

translations.literal: The people of Baoshan, hearing the news, trembled; they bound the criminals to welcome the army, executed the chief culprits, dispersed the coerced followers, and summoned Han and Hui elders to instruct them with grace and sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Baoshan were terrified when they heard of his approach; they bound up the culprits to welcome his army, he executed the ringleaders and released those who had been coerced, and he summoned Han and Hui community elders to reassure them with pledges of mercy and good faith.

sentences.zh: 遂搜捕永昌、順寧、雲州、姚州歷年戕官諸重犯，威德震洽，邊境乃安。

translations.literal: He then searched out and arrested the major criminals in Yongchang, Shunning, Yunzhou, and Yaozhou who over the years had killed officials; his authority and kindness filled the land, and the frontier was then at peace.
translations.idiomatic: He then tracked down and arrested major offenders in Yongchang, Shunning, Yunzhou, and Yaozhou who had killed officials over the years; his prestige and humane rule won universal respect, and the borderlands were finally pacified.

sentences.zh: 加太子太保，賜花翎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and granted the peacock feather plume.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and awarded the peacock feather insignia.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，騰越邊外野夷滋擾，遣兵平之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, wild tribes beyond the Tengyue border caused renewed disturbances, and he dispatched troops to pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: In 1849 unruly tribal peoples beyond the Tengyue frontier again harassed the border, and he sent troops to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 以病乞歸。

translations.literal: He cited illness and requested leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned on grounds of illness and returned home.

sentences.zh: 逾年，文宗嗣位，疊詔宣召，未至，以廣西逆首洪秀全稔亂，授欽差大臣，督師進剿，並署廣西巡撫。

translations.literal: After a year the Wenzong Emperor succeeded to the throne; repeated edicts summoned him, but before he arrived, because the Guangxi rebel leader Hong Xiuquan had long been in rebellion, he was appointed imperial commissioner to supervise troops in the campaign of suppression and also to act as Guangxi governor.
translations.idiomatic: A year later, when the Xianfeng Emperor ascended the throne, repeated summonses reached him, but before he could arrive, Hong Xiuquan—the rebel leader in Guangxi—had entrenched his uprising; Lin was appointed imperial commissioner to lead the suppression and was also named acting governor of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 行次潮州，病卒。

translations.literal: En route, at Chaozhou, he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness at Chaozhou while still on the road.

sentences.zh: 則徐威惠久著南服，賊聞其出，皆震悚，中道遽歿，天下惜之。

translations.literal: Zexu's authority and kindness had long been renowned in the southern regions; when rebels heard he was setting out, they were all shaken and fearful, but he died suddenly en route, and the empire mourned his loss.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Zexu had long been famed throughout the south for his stern justice and humane rule; when bandits heard he was coming, they were seized with fear, but his sudden death on the march was mourned throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 遺疏上，優詔賜卹，贈太子太傅，諡文忠。

translations.literal: His death memorial was submitted; a favorable edict granted mourning compensation, posthumously appointing him Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent with the posthumous title Wenzhong.
translations.idiomatic: His final memorial reached the throne; the court issued a generous edict of condolence, posthumously ennobling him as Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent with the posthumous name Wenzhong.

sentences.zh: 雲南、江蘇並祀名宦，陝西請建專祠。

translations.literal: Yunnan and Jiangsu both enshrined him among famous officials; Shaanxi requested a dedicated shrine.
translations.idiomatic: Yunnan and Jiangsu both added him to their shrines to eminent local officials, while Shaanxi petitioned to build a temple devoted to him alone.

sentences.zh: 則徐才識過人，而待下虛衷，人樂為用，所蒞治績皆卓越。

translations.literal: Zexu's talent and insight surpassed others, yet he treated subordinates with open sincerity; people gladly served him, and in every post he governed his achievements were outstanding.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Zexu's ability far outstripped that of his peers, yet he treated subordinates with sincere openness, so that men were eager to work for him; in every office he held, his administrative record was exemplary.

sentences.zh: 道光之季，東南困於漕運，宣宗密詢利弊，疏陳補救本原諸策，上畿輔水利議，文宗欲命籌辦而未果。

translations.literal: In the late Daoguang period the southeast was afflicted by the grain transport system; the Daoguang Emperor secretly inquired into advantages and drawbacks, and he memorialized various policies to remedy fundamental causes and submitted a proposal on water conservancy in the capital region; the Xianfeng Emperor wished to assign him to plan it but the matter did not come to pass.
translations.idiomatic: In the closing years of the Daoguang reign the southeast was crippled by the grain-shipping system; the emperor privately asked his views on the trade-offs, and Lin submitted a series of memorials on fundamental remedies along with a plan for waterworks in the metropolitan region—the Xianfeng Emperor intended to put him in charge of carrying it out, but the plan was never realized.

sentences.zh: 海疆事起，時以英吉利最強為憂，則徐獨曰：「為中國患者，其俄羅斯乎！

translations.literal: When maritime frontier troubles arose, people at the time worried most that England was the strongest; Zexu alone said, "The one who will afflict China—is it not Russia?
translations.idiomatic: When trouble erupted along the coast, contemporaries chiefly feared England as the strongest power; Lin Zexu alone remarked, "The power that will truly menace China—is it not Russia?

sentences.zh: 」後其言果驗。

translations.literal: Later his words indeed proved true.
translations.idiomatic: His prediction would later prove correct.

sentences.zh: 鄧廷楨 鄧廷楨，字嶰筠，江蘇江寧人。

translations.literal: Deng Tingzhen. Deng Tingzhen, styled Xieyun, was a native of Jiangning in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Tingzhen. Deng Tingzhen, courtesy name Xieyun, was a native of Jiangning in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶六年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Jiaqing he became a jinshi, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In 1801 he passed the metropolitan examination, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and was appointed a compiler.

sentences.zh: 屢分校鄉、會試，稱得士。

translations.literal: He repeatedly served as examiner for the provincial and metropolitan examinations and was praised for selecting worthy scholars.
translations.idiomatic: He served repeatedly as an examiner for the provincial and metropolitan examinations and gained a reputation for recognizing talented men.

sentences.zh: 十五年，授台灣遺缺知府，浙江巡撫蔣攸銛請留浙，補寧波。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was appointed magistrate to fill a Taiwan vacancy; the Zhejiang governor Jiang Youqian requested that he remain in Zhejiang, and he was appointed to Ningbo.
translations.idiomatic: In 1810 he was slated to fill a vacant prefecture in Taiwan, but Zhejiang governor Jiang Youqian asked to keep him in the province, and he was posted instead to Ningbo.

sentences.zh: 母憂歸，服闋，補陝西延安府，歷榆林、西安，以善折獄稱。

translations.literal: He returned home for his mother's mourning; after the mourning period ended he was appointed to Yan'an Prefecture in Shaanxi, served successively at Yulin and Xi'an, and was known for skill in deciding cases.
translations.idiomatic: After he went home to observe mourning for his mother and the mourning period ended, he was appointed prefect of Yan'an in Shaanxi, later served at Yulin and Xi'an, and won renown for his skill in resolving legal disputes.

sentences.zh: 平反韓城、南鄭冤獄，又全同州嫠婦母子，陝民歌頌，傳播京師。

translations.literal: He overturned wrongful convictions at Hancheng and Nanzheng, and also preserved the lives of a Tongzhou widow and her child; the people of Shaanxi sang his praises, and the story spread to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He reversed wrongful convictions at Hancheng and Nanzheng and also saved a widow and her son at Tongzhou from injustice; the people of Shaanxi celebrated him in song, and word of his deeds reached Beijing.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，超擢湖北按察使，權布政使。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he was exceptionally promoted to Hubei surveillance commissioner and acted as provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: In 1820 he was given an exceptional promotion to surveillance commissioner of Hubei and served concurrently as acting financial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 沿江民田歷年沈沒，而賦額仍在，為民累，悉請免之。

translations.literal: Along the river, civilian fields had been submerged for many years while the tax quota still stood, becoming a burden on the people; he requested that all be exempted.
translations.idiomatic: Farmland along the river had lain submerged for years while tax quotas remained unchanged, imposing a heavy burden on the populace; he petitioned to have all such levies waived.

sentences.zh: 道光元年，遷江西布政使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daoguang he was transferred to Jiangxi provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: In 1821 he was transferred to the post of financial commissioner of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 以前在西安失察渭南令故出縣民柳全璧殺人罪，罣誤，奪職。

translations.literal: Because while in Xi'an he had failed to oversee the Weinan magistrate who had improperly released the county man Liu Quanbi from a homicide charge, he was implicated in the error and stripped of his post.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed because, while serving in Xi'an, he had failed to detect that the magistrate of Weinan had unlawfully freed a local man named Liu Quanbi from a murder charge.

sentences.zh: 議戍軍台，宣宗知其無私，特免遣戍，予七品銜，發直隸委用。

translations.literal: It was proposed that he be exiled to a military post; the Daoguang Emperor knew he had no private motive, specially exempted him from exile, granted him seventh-rank status, and assigned him for service in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Exile to a garrison station was proposed, but the Daoguang Emperor knew he had acted without personal bias and specially spared him from banishment, granting him seventh-rank status and assigning him for duty in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 尋授通永道。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed intendant of the Tongzhou-Yongding Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon named intendant of the Tongzhou-Yongding Circuit.

sentences.zh: 四年，擢陝西按察使，遷布政使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was promoted to Shaanxi surveillance commissioner and transferred to provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: In 1824 he was promoted to surveillance commissioner of Shaanxi and then transferred to financial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 六年，擢安徽巡撫。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was promoted to Anhui governor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1826 he was appointed governor of Anhui.

sentences.zh: 自嘉慶時，安徽多大獄，鳳、潁兩郡俗尤悍，常以兵定，責繳兵械，私藏尚多。

translations.literal: Since the Jiaqing era Anhui had many major cases; the customs of the two prefectures Feng and Ying were especially fierce, and disturbances were often settled by troops; they were ordered to surrender weapons, yet many remained privately hoarded.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Jiaqing reign Anhui had seen many major criminal cases; the folkways of Feng and Ying prefectures were especially violent, and the authorities had repeatedly had to resort to troops; weapons were ordered turned in, but many were still hidden in private hands.

sentences.zh: 廷楨乃立限，責成保長，逾限及私造者置之法。

translations.literal: Tingzhen then set deadlines, holding baojia chiefs responsible; those who exceeded the deadline and those who privately manufactured weapons were punished according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Deng set firm deadlines and held local baojia leaders accountable; anyone who missed the deadline or manufactured arms privately was prosecuted.

sentences.zh: 任吏皆得人，刁悍之風稍戢。

translations.literal: The officials he appointed were all capable men, and the fierce and unruly temper gradually subsided.
translations.idiomatic: He staffed his administration with capable officials, and the region's lawlessness gradually eased.

sentences.zh: 舊例，潁州屬三人以上凶器傷人者，極邊煙瘴充軍，僉妻發配。

translations.literal: Under the old regulation, in the Yingzhou jurisdiction when three or more persons injured others with deadly weapons, they were exiled to the farthest malarial frontier as soldiers, and their wives were collectively sent into exile.
translations.idiomatic: Under existing rules, when three or more persons in Yingzhou jurisdiction wounded someone with a lethal weapon, the offenders were exiled as convict soldiers to the remotest malarial frontier and their wives were deported with them.

sentences.zh: 廷楨疏言：「悍俗誠宜重懲，婦女顧名節，多自殘求免，或自盡傷生，情在可矜，請停其例。

translations.literal: Tingzhen memorialized, saying, "The fierce customs truly ought to be heavily punished, but women value their chastity and often mutilate themselves to seek exemption, or kill themselves and harm their lives; the circumstances are pitiable—please suspend this regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Deng memorialized, saying, "Such violent customs truly deserve severe punishment, but women cherish their reputation for chastity; many mutilate themselves to escape deportation, or take their own lives and wound others in the process—these cases merit compassion, and I ask that this regulation be suspended.

sentences.zh: 」遇水災，親乘舟勘賑。

translations.literal: Encountering flooding, he personally boarded a boat to inspect disaster relief.
translations.idiomatic: When floods struck, he personally took to a boat to survey relief work.

sentences.zh: 修復安豐塘、芍陂水門，濬鳳陽沫河，加築堤閘。

translations.literal: He restored the Anfeng Pond and the sluice gates of Shaopi, dredged the Mo River at Fengyang, and strengthened dikes and sluice gates.
translations.idiomatic: He restored the Anfeng Pond and the water gates of the Shaopi reservoir, dredged the Mo River in Fengyang, and reinforced embankments and floodgates.

sentences.zh: 嚴緝捕，屢獲劇盜。

translations.literal: He enforced strict pursuit and capture and repeatedly seized major bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He tightened pursuit of criminals and captured numerous major bandits.

sentences.zh: 以獲南河掘堤首犯陳端，詔嘉獎。

translations.literal: Because he captured Chen Duan, the chief culprit who had dug through the South River dike, an edict praised and rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: When he captured Chen Duan, the principal culprit behind the deliberate breach of the South River embankment, the court issued an edict of commendation.

sentences.zh: 治皖十載，政尚安靜，境內大和。

translations.literal: He governed Anhui for ten years; his policy favored tranquility, and within the borders there was great peace.
translations.idiomatic: Over ten years in Anhui he pursued a policy of quiet governance, and the province enjoyed widespread peace.

sentences.zh: 十五年，擢兩廣總督。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was promoted to governor-general of Guangdong-Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In 1835 he was appointed governor-general of Guangdong and Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 鴉片煙方盛行，漏銀出洋為大患。

translations.literal: Opium smoking was then flourishing, and the outflow of silver overseas was a great calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Opium smoking was rampant, and the drain of silver abroad had become a grave national crisis.

sentences.zh: 十六年，英吉利商人以躉船載煙，廷楨禁止不許進口，猶泊外洋，嚴旨驅逐。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, English merchants carried opium on receiving ships; Tingzhen forbade import, but they still moored on the outer sea until a stern edict ordered their expulsion.
translations.idiomatic: In 1836 British merchants brought opium on storeships; Deng banned importation, but the vessels still lay offshore until a stern imperial order drove them away.

sentences.zh: 沿海奸民勾結，禁令猝難斷絕。

translations.literal: Coastal wicked persons colluded with them, and the prohibition could not suddenly be completely severed.
translations.idiomatic: Coastal smugglers were in league with them, and the ban could not be enforced overnight.

sentences.zh: 廷楨與提督關天培整備海防，迭於大嶼山口、急水洋獲蟹艇，載銀鉅萬，盡數充賞，破獲囤煙私販。

translations.literal: Tingzhen and the provincial commander Guan Tianpei readied coastal defenses; repeatedly at Dachu Pass and Jishuiyang they seized smuggling craft, with silver in the tens of thousands, all confiscated and distributed as rewards, and broke up hoarded opium and private sellers.
translations.idiomatic: Deng and naval commander Guan Tianpei strengthened coastal defenses; they repeatedly seized smuggling boats at Dachu Pass and Jishuiyang carrying vast sums in silver, confiscated the entire haul for distribution as rewards, and broke up stockpiles of opium and private trafficking rings.

sentences.zh: 十八年，英船載屬番男婦五百餘人赴澳門居住，驅令回國。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, English ships brought more than five hundred subject tribesmen, men and women, to live at Macao; he drove them to return to their country.
translations.idiomatic: In 1838 British ships brought more than five hundred dependent subjects—men, women, and children—to settle at Macao; he ordered them sent back to their homelands.

sentences.zh: 詔下禁煙議，疏言：「法行於豪貴，則小民易從；

translations.literal: When an edict was issued on the opium prohibition debate, he memorialized, saying, "When the law is applied among the powerful and noble, the common people are easily made to follow;
translations.idiomatic: When the court circulated plans for suppressing opium, he memorialized, saying, "When the law is enforced against the wealthy and powerful, ordinary people will readily comply;

sentences.zh: 令嚴於中土，則外貨自絀。

translations.literal: when regulations are strict within China, foreign goods will naturally be suppressed.
translations.idiomatic: when prohibition is strict within the empire, foreign opium will dry up of itself.

sentences.zh: 」十九年，林則徐奉命至廣東，廷楨與之同心協力，盡獲躉船積煙，焚之，嚴私販之罪；

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year Lin Zexu was ordered to Guangdong; Tingzhen united with him in single purpose, seized all opium accumulated on receiving ships, burned it, and imposed severe penalties for private trafficking;
translations.idiomatic: In 1839 Lin Zexu reached Guangdong on imperial commission; Deng cooperated with him wholeheartedly, seized every hoard of opium on the storeships, burned it, and imposed severe punishments on smugglers;

sentences.zh: 臨以兵威，屢戰皆捷，事詳則徐傳。

translations.literal: They confronted [the enemy] with military might; battle after battle was won—the particulars are given in the biography of Lin Zexu.
translations.idiomatic: They confronted the enemy with military force and won victory after victory; the fuller account appears in the biography of Lin Zexu.

sentences.zh: 奸民因失業，遍騰蜚語。

translations.literal: Wicked commoners, having lost their livelihoods, spread slanderous rumors everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: Displaced smugglers and criminals, thrown out of work, spread malicious rumors throughout the region.

sentences.zh: 廷楨疏陳，略曰：「臣緝懲鴉片，三載於茲。

translations.literal: Tingzhen memorialized the throne, stating in summary: "Your servant has prosecuted and punished opium for three years now.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Tingzhen submitted a memorial that read, in part: "Your servant has pursued the opium trade and punished offenders for three years now.

sentences.zh: 豪猾之徒，刑僇逋逃，身家既失，怨讟遂興。

translations.literal: The powerful and cunning sort, punished and put to flight, having lost their families and fortunes, gave rise to complaints and slander.
translations.idiomatic: Powerful rackets and cunning traffickers were flogged and driven into hiding; stripped of homes and livelihoods, they nursed grievances and spread recrimination.

sentences.zh: 查檢為希旨，掩捕為貪功，偵伺為詭謀，推​​鞫為酷罰。

translations.literal: Inspection was called currying favor; covert arrest was called grasping for merit; surveillance was called scheming; interrogation was called cruel punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Customs searches became "currying favor with Beijing"; roundups became "grasping for credit"; surveillance became "intrigue"; and inquests became "torture."

sentences.zh: 誣以納賄，目以營私。

translations.literal: They slandered [us] as taking bribes; they labeled [us] as pursuing private gain.
translations.idiomatic: They charged us with taking bribes and accused us of pursuing private profit.

sentences.zh: 譏建議為急於理財，訾新例為輕於改律，狂悖紛熒，無非為煙匪洩憤。

translations.literal: They mocked proposals as haste to raise revenue; they denounced new regulations as lightly altering the laws—wild and rebellious clamor, all nothing but opium traffickers venting their rage.
translations.idiomatic: They mocked reform proposals as a rush to raise revenue and denounced new regulations as reckless changes to the law—reckless, contradictory outcry, all of it nothing but opium traffickers venting their spite.

sentences.zh: 」詔慰勉之。

translations.literal: " An edict comforted and encouraged him.
translations.idiomatic: The throne issued an edict of consolation and encouragement.

sentences.zh: 調兩江、雲貴，皆未赴，閩防方急，遂調閩浙總督。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Two Jiangs and Yun-Gui [posts], but went to neither; as Fujian's defense was urgent, he was then made Governor-General of Fujian-Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to the Two Jiangs and to Yun-Gui but took neither post; with Fujian's coastal defense urgent, he was appointed governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 購洋砲十四運閩，以閩洋無內港，砲台建於海灘，沙浮不固，奏改為砲墩，囊沙堆築，外護以船。

translations.literal: He purchased fourteen shipments of foreign cannon for Fujian; because Fujian's seas had no inner harbors and batteries built on the beach were unstable in drifting sand, he memorialized to replace them with gun emplacements—sandbag mounds, shielded outward by boats.
translations.idiomatic: He procured fourteen shiploads of Western cannon for Fujian. Because Fujian's coast lacks sheltered inner harbors and beach-built batteries rest on shifting sand, he petitioned to replace them with sand-filled gun platforms shielded by vessels moored offshore.

sentences.zh: 募水勇飾商船出洋巡緝。

translations.literal: He recruited naval braves, fitted out merchant ships, and sent them out to sea to patrol and suppress [smuggling].
translations.idiomatic: He recruited naval militia, armed merchant vessels, and dispatched them to patrol and interdict traffickers offshore.

sentences.zh: 二十年三月，英船窺廈門，遣提督程恩高等迎敵於梅林澳，擊走之。

translations.literal: In the third month of the twentieth year, British ships reconnoitered Xiamen; he sent Provincial Commander Cheng Engao and others to meet the enemy at Meilin Bay and drive them off.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the twentieth year, British vessels scouted Xiamen; he sent Provincial Commander Cheng Engao and others to meet them at Meilin Bay and drive them off.

sentences.zh: 奸民勾通出洋運煙，分責水陸師嚴緝，遇即攻擊，迭有殲擒。

translations.literal: Wicked commoners colluded to carry opium out to sea; he assigned strict joint pursuit to land and naval forces—on encounter they attacked at once, repeatedly killing and capturing [smugglers].
translations.idiomatic: Wicked natives colluded to carry opium out to sea; he ordered land and naval forces to pursue them rigorously, attacking on sight and repeatedly killing and capturing smugglers.

sentences.zh: 六月，敵船駛入廈門，求通貿易，阻之，遂開砲，來撲砲台，參將陳勝元、守備陳光福奮擊，斃其前隊數人，發砲傷敵甚眾，乃遁。

translations.literal: In the sixth month enemy ships entered Xiamen, seeking to trade; blocked, they opened fire and came to storm the batteries; Deputy Commander Chen Shengyuan and Garrison Commander Chen Guangfu fought back fiercely, killing several of the van and wounding the enemy in great numbers with cannon fire, whereupon [the enemy] fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month enemy ships entered Xiamen demanding trade; blocked, they opened fire and rushed the batteries. Deputy Commander Chen Shengyuan and Garrison Commander Chen Guangfu fought back fiercely, killing several of the van and inflicting heavy losses with cannon fire, after which the enemy fled.

sentences.zh: 其分犯浙洋者，陷定海，廷楨率師赴剿，行次清風嶺，詔以閩防緊要，止其赴浙，遂駐兵泉州，招募練勇。

translations.literal: Those who raided Zhejiang waters in a separate column took Dinghai; Tingzhen led troops to suppress them, but at Qingfeng Ridge an edict, citing the urgent need in Fujian, halted his going to Zhejiang; he therefore camped troops at Quanzhou and recruited drilled braves.
translations.idiomatic: When separate columns raided Zhejiang waters and took Dinghai, Tingzhen led troops to suppress them, but at Qingfeng Ridge an edict, citing the urgent need in Fujian, halted his march to Zhejiang; he therefore camped at Quanzhou and recruited drilled militia.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「英船二十餘艘聚泊定海，內地師船恐難驟近，必改造堅大之船，多配砲火，間道而進，方能制勝。

translations.literal: In a memorial he said: "More than twenty British ships are gathered at Dinghai; inland war-junks probably cannot close on them suddenly—we must build stout, large ships, arm them heavily with cannon, and advance by devious routes before we can win."
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he wrote that more than twenty British vessels lay at Dinghai and inland war-junks could hardly close suddenly—only by building stout, large ships, arming them heavily, and advancing by devious routes could victory be won.

sentences.zh: 」 九月，詔以廷楨等在粵辦理不善，轉滋事端，與林則徐同奪職。

translations.literal: " In the ninth month an edict blamed Tingzhen and others for mismanaging affairs at Guangdong and provoking trouble, and stripped them of office together with Lin Zexu.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month an edict blamed Deng Tingzhen and others for mismanaging affairs at Guangdong and provoking trouble, and stripped them of office along with Lin Zexu.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，琦善撤沿海兵備，虎門失守，复追論廷楨久任兩廣，廢弛營務，與則徐同戍伊犁。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year Qi Shan withdrew coastal defenses; Humen fell; [the court] again condemned Tingzhen for long service in the Two Guangs and neglected camps, and banished him with Lin Zexu to Yili.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year Qi Shan withdrew coastal defenses and Humen fell; Deng Tingzhen was again condemned for long service in Guangdong and neglected camps, and was banished with Lin Zexu to Yili.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，釋還。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he was released and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he was released and returned.

sentences.zh: 尋予三品頂戴，授甘肅布政使。

translations.literal: Soon he was given a third-rank button and appointed Financial Commissioner of Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was given a third-rank button and appointed financial commissioner of Gansu.

sentences.zh: 議清查荒地，親往歷勘，由銀州東盡洮、隴，西極酒泉，得田一萬九千四百餘頃，又番貢地一千五百餘頃，寧夏馬廠地歸公一百餘頃，熟地昇科，荒者招墾，詔嘉其勤，复二品頂戴。

translations.literal: He proposed to investigate and clear barren land and went in person on inspection; from east of Yinchuan through Tao and Long to Jiuquan in the west he registered more than 19,400 qing of fields, plus over 1,500 qing of tribute frontier land and more than 100 qing of Ningxia pasture returned to the state; cultivated land was brought under tax, waste land was opened to settlement—an edict praised his diligence and restored his second-rank button.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed to survey and register wasteland and went in person to inspect it, from east of Yinchuan through Tao and Long to Jiuquan in the west, registering more than 19,400 qing of fields, plus over 1,500 qing of tribute frontier land and more than 100 qing of Ningxia pasture returned to the state; cultivated land was brought under tax and waste land opened to settlement, and the throne praised his diligence and restored his second-rank button.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，擢陝西巡撫，署陝甘總督。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he was promoted to Governor of Shaanxi and acted as Governor-General of Shaanxi-Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year he was promoted to governor of Shaanxi and acted as governor-general of Shaanxi-Gansu.

sentences.zh: 番匪擾蒙部，遣兵邀擊於硫磺溝，平之。

translations.literal: Frontier tribesmen disturbed the Mongol banners; he sent troops to intercept them at Liuhuang Gully and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: When frontier tribesmen disturbed the Mongol banners, he sent troops to intercept them at Liuhuang Gully and pacified the disturbance.

sentences.zh: 尋回任。

translations.literal: Soon he resumed his regular post.
translations.idiomatic: He soon resumed his regular post.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，卒於官。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year he died in office.

sentences.zh: 廷楨治行早為時稱，屢躓屢起，宣宗知之深，故卒用之。

translations.literal: Tingzhen's conduct in office had long been praised; though he stumbled and rose again many times, the Xuanzong Emperor knew him deeply and therefore employed him to the end.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Tingzhen's conduct had long been praised; though he stumbled and rose again many times, the Xuanzong Emperor knew him well and therefore employed him to the end.

sentences.zh: 績學好士，幕府多名流，論學不輟。

translations.literal: Deeply learned and fond of scholars, his staff housed many eminent men, and he never ceased discoursing on learning.
translations.idiomatic: He was deeply learned and fond of scholars; his staff housed many eminent men, and he never ceased discoursing on learning.

sentences.zh: 尤精於音韻之學，所著筆記、詩、詞並行世。

translations.literal: He was especially expert in the study of phonology; his notebooks, verse, and lyrics all circulated in his day.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially expert in phonology; his notebooks, verse, and lyrics circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 子爾恆，亦官至陝西巡撫，自有傳。

translations.literal: His son Erheng also rose to Governor of Shaanxi and has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Erheng also rose to governor of Shaanxi and has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 當廷楨之去福建也，逾年，英兵復至，陷廈門，遂窺台灣。

translations.literal: When Tingzhen left Fujian, a year later the British returned, took Xiamen, and then turned toward Taiwan.
translations.idiomatic: When Deng Tingzhen left Fujian, a year later the British returned, seized Xiamen, and then turned toward Taiwan.

sentences.zh: 總兵達洪阿偕台灣道姚瑩屢卻之。

translations.literal: Brigade Commander Da Hong'a together with Taiwan Intendant Yao Ying repeatedly repulsed them.
translations.idiomatic: Brigade Commander Da Hong'a together with Taiwan Intendant Yao Ying repeatedly repulsed them.

sentences.zh: 及和議成，同獲譴。

translations.literal: When the peace was concluded, both were punished.
translations.idiomatic: After the peace was concluded, both were punished.

sentences.zh: 達洪阿 達洪阿，字厚庵，富察氏，滿洲鑲黃旗人。

translations.literal: Da Hong'a—Da Hong'a, styled Hou'an, of the Fuca clan, a Manchu of the Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Da Hong'a, styled Hou'an, of the Fuca clan, was a Bannerman of the Bordered Yellow.

sentences.zh: 由護軍洊擢總兵。

translations.literal: From guardsman he was steadily promoted to brigade commander.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from guardsman to brigade commander by steady promotion.

sentences.zh: 道光十五年，調台灣鎮。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Daoguang he was transferred to Taiwan Brigade.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Daoguang he was transferred to Taiwan Brigade.

sentences.zh: 十八年，剿嘉義縣匪沈和等，賜花翎，加提督銜。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he suppressed the bandits Shen He and others in Jiayi County, was awarded the peacock feather, and given the nominal rank of provincial commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he suppressed the bandit Shen He and others in Jiayi County, was awarded the peacock feather, and given the nominal rank of provincial commander.

sentences.zh: 二十一年八月，英兵船至雞籠海口，達洪阿與姚瑩督兵御之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the twenty-first year, British warships reached the harbor of Keelung; Da Hong'a with Yao Ying directed troops in defense.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the twenty-first year, when British ships reached the harbor of Keelung, Da Hong'a with Yao Ying directed troops in defense.

sentences.zh: 副將邱鎮功燃巨砲折其桅，敵船衝礁破碎，擒斬甚眾，賜雙眼花翎。

translations.literal: Deputy Commander Qiu Zhengong fired a great gun that broke their mast; an enemy ship struck a reef and was shattered, and many were killed or captured—he was given the double peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy Commander Qiu Zhengong fired a great gun that broke their mast; an enemy ship struck a reef and was shattered, and many were killed or captured—he was awarded the double peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 九月，敵船再至雞籠三沙灣，复卻之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month enemy ships came again to Sansha Bay at Keelung and were again repulsed.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month enemy ships came again to Sansha Bay at Keelung and were again repulsed.

sentences.zh: 剿平嘉義、鳳山土匪，予騎都尉世職。

translations.literal: He pacified bandits in Jiayi and Fengshan and was granted the hereditary rank of Cavalry Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He pacified bandits in Jiayi and Fengshan and was granted the hereditary rank of Cavalry Commandant.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，敵船犯淡水、彰化間之大安港，欲入口。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year enemy ships threatened Da'an Harbor between Tamsui and Changhua, intending to enter port.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year enemy ships threatened Da'an Harbor between Tamsui and Changhua, intending to enter port.

sentences.zh: 達洪阿謀於姚瑩，瑩曰：「此未可與海上爭鋒，必以計殲之。

translations.literal: Da Hong'a consulted Yao Ying; Ying said: "We cannot contest them on the open sea—we must destroy them by stratagem."
translations.idiomatic: Da Hong'a consulted Yao Ying, who said, "We cannot contest them on the open sea; they must be destroyed by stratagem."

sentences.zh: 」乃募漁舟投敵任鄉導，誘令從土地公港入，擱淺中流，伏發，大破之，落水死者無算，其竄入漁舟者，擊斬殆盡。

translations.literal: " They then recruited fishing boats to pose as guides for the enemy, lured them to enter by the Tudi Gong port, grounded them midstream, and with ambush troops opened fire and broke them utterly—those who fell into the water died beyond counting; those who scrambled into fishing boats were killed or beheaded nearly to the last man.
translations.idiomatic: They recruited fishing boats to pose as enemy guides and lured the fleet to enter by the Tudi Gong port, where the ships grounded midstream; troops lying in ambush opened fire and broke them completely—countless drowned, and those who scrambled into fishing boats were nearly all killed or captured.

sentences.zh: 詔嘉台灣三次破敵，達洪阿等智勇兼施，大揚國威，賜號阿克達春巴圖魯，加太子太保銜。

translations.literal: An edict praised Taiwan's three victories over the enemy, declaring that Da Hong'a and others had combined wisdom and courage to glorify the national prestige; he was granted the title Akdachun Baturu and the nominal rank of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: An edict praised Taiwan's three victories, declaring that Da Hong'a and others had combined courage and cunning to glorify the realm; he was granted the title Akdachun Baturu and the nominal rank of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 敵船遊奕外洋，乘間掩擊，迭有俘獲，遂不復至。

translations.literal: Enemy ships roamed the outer sea; [our forces] seized opportunities for surprise attacks and repeatedly took captives, whereupon [the enemy] did not return.
translations.idiomatic: Enemy ships roamed the outer sea, but surprise attacks whenever opportunity offered yielded repeated captures, and they did not return.

sentences.zh: 既而英師再陷定海，浙江、江蘇軍屢挫，乃議和。

translations.literal: Soon the British army again took Dinghai; the armies of Zhejiang and Jiangsu suffered repeated defeats, and peace was negotiated.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the British again took Dinghai; armies of Zhejiang and Jiangsu suffered repeated defeats, and peace was negotiated.

sentences.zh: 英將濮鼎查訴稱台灣所戮皆遭風難民，達洪阿等冒功捏奏，命總督怡良赴台灣查辦。

translations.literal: British commander Pottinger complained that those killed in Taiwan were all sufferers from shipwreck; Da Hong'a and others had falsely claimed merit and fabricated memorials—the court ordered Governor Yilibu to go to Taiwan to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: British commander Pottinger complained that those killed in Taiwan were only shipwrecked sufferers; Da Hong'a and others had falsely claimed merit and fabricated memorials, and the court ordered Governor Yilibu to go to Taiwan to investigate.

sentences.zh: 至即傳旨革職逮問，兵民不服，勢洶洶，達洪阿等撫慰乃散。

translations.literal: Upon his arrival an edict was transmitted stripping them of office for interrogation; soldiers and civilians were discontent and the mood grew menacing—Da Hong'a and others comforted them and [the crowd] dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Upon his arrival an edict arrived stripping them of office for interrogation; soldiers and civilians were indignant and the mood grew menacing until Da Hong'a and others calmed them and the crowd dispersed.

sentences.zh: 至京，下刑部獄，尋釋之，予三等侍衛，充哈密辦事大臣。

translations.literal: Reaching the capital, he was sent to the Ministry of Punishments prison; soon released, he was made a third-class bodyguard and appointed Minister Superintendent at Hami.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching the capital, he was sent to the Ministry of Punishments, soon released, made a third-class bodyguard, and appointed minister superintendent at Hami.

sentences.zh: 歷伊犁參贊大臣，西寧辦事大臣。

translations.literal: He later served as Assistant at Ili and Minister Superintendent at Xining.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as assistant at Ili and minister superintendent at Xining.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，偕陝甘總督布彥泰剿平黑錯寺番匪。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, together with Shaanxi-Gansu Governor-General Buyantai, he suppressed and pacified the tribal rebels of Heicuo Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In 1846 he joined Governor-General Buyantai of Shaanxi and Gansu in suppressing the tribal rebels at Heicuo Temple.

sentences.zh: 三十年，授副都統。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he was appointed deputy lieutenant-general.
translations.idiomatic: In 1850 he was appointed deputy lieutenant-general.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，從大學士賽尚阿勦賊廣西，破紫金山西南砲台。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng he followed Grand Secretary Saincha'a to suppress rebels in Guangxi and captured the southwest batteries of Zijin Hill.
translations.idiomatic: In 1851 he followed Grand Secretary Saincha'a to campaign against the rebels in Guangxi and captured the batteries on the southwest slope of Zijin Hill.

sentences.zh: 以病回京。

translations.literal: He returned to the capital on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Illness forced him to return to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 三年，粵匪犯畿輔，率八旗兵赴臨洺關進剿。

translations.literal: In the third year Cantonese rebels invaded the capital region; he led Eight Banner troops to Linming Pass to advance against them.
translations.idiomatic: In 1853, when Cantonese rebels threatened the capital region, he led Eight Banner troops to Linming Pass to attack them.

sentences.zh: 從欽差大臣勝保擊賊靜海，四戰皆捷，追至下西河，副都統佟鑑、天津知縣謝子澄陣亡。

translations.literal: Following Imperial Commissioner Senggelinqin he attacked rebels at Jinghai, won victory in four engagements, pursued them to Xiaxihe, and Deputy Lieutenant-General Tong Jian and Tianjin magistrate Xie Zicheng fell in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Serving under Imperial Commissioner Senggelinqin, he fought the rebels at Jinghai, won four successive engagements, and pursued them to Xiaxihe, where Deputy Lieutenant-General Tong Jian and Tianjin magistrate Xie Zicheng were killed in action.

sentences.zh: 詔斥達洪阿先退，革職，留營效力。

translations.literal: An edict rebuked Da Hong'a for retreating first, dismissed him from office, and ordered him to remain with the army to redeem himself.
translations.idiomatic: An edict blamed Da Hong'a for retreating prematurely, stripped him of office, and ordered him to remain with the army to redeem himself.

sentences.zh: 四年，敗賊獻縣，復原官。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he defeated rebels at Xian County and was restored to his former rank.
translations.idiomatic: In 1854 he defeated rebels at Xian County and was restored to his former rank.

sentences.zh: 尋追賊阜城，受傷，卒於軍。

translations.literal: Soon after, pursuing rebels at Fucheng, he was wounded and died in camp.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, while pursuing rebels at Fucheng, he was wounded and died in camp.

sentences.zh: 贈都統銜，予騎都尉兼一云騎尉世職，諡壯武。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given the rank of lieutenant-general, granted the hereditary offices of Cavalry Commandant with one additional Cloud Cavalry Commandant, and given the posthumous title Zhuangwu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously promoted to lieutenant-general, granted the hereditary titles of Cavalry Commandant with an additional Cloud Cavalry Commandant, and given the posthumous name Zhuangwu.

sentences.zh: 姚瑩自有傳。

translations.literal: Yao Ying has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Ying has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 論曰：林則徐才略冠時，禁煙一役，承宣宗嚴切之旨，操之過急；

translations.literal: The judgment says: Lin Zexu's talent and strategy topped his age; in the opium prohibition campaign he carried out the Xuanzong Emperor's stern and urgent will, but handled matters too hastily;
translations.idiomatic: The historians comment: Lin Zexu's ability stood above his contemporaries; in the opium suppression he carried out Emperor Daoguang's stern orders, yet pressed the campaign too hard;

sentences.zh: 及敵氛蹈瑕他犯，遂遭讒屏斥。

translations.literal: when the enemy seized on flaws and struck elsewhere, he then suffered slander and dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: when the enemy exploited openings and struck elsewhere, he fell victim to slander and removal.

sentences.zh: 論者謂粵事始終倚之，加之操縱，潰裂當不致此。

translations.literal: Commentators say that Guangdong affairs throughout relied on him, and that with him in control the collapse need not have reached this point.
translations.idiomatic: Some argue that Guangdong had always depended on him and that, had he remained in command, the collapse might never have occurred.

sentences.zh: 則徐瀕謫，疏陳：「自道光元年以來，粵關徵銀三千餘萬兩，收其利必防其害。

translations.literal: On the verge of dismissal Lin memorialized: "Since the first year of Daoguang, the Guangdong customs have collected more than thirty million taels of silver; in taking the profit one must guard against the harm."
translations.idiomatic: Facing dismissal, Lin memorialized: "Since 1821 the Guangdong customs have collected more than thirty million taels of silver; those who reap the profit must also guard against the harm."

sentences.zh: 使以關稅十分之一制砲造船，制夷已可裕如。

translations.literal: If one used one-tenth of the customs revenue to build cannon and ships, controlling the foreigners would already be ample.
translations.idiomatic: Had one-tenth of customs revenue been spent on cannon and ships, keeping the foreigners in check would have been ample.

sentences.zh: 」誠為讜論。

translations.literal: This was truly sound counsel.
translations.idiomatic: That was sound counsel indeed.

sentences.zh: 惟當時內治廢弛，外情隔膜，言和言戰，皆昧機宜，其禍豈能倖免哉？

translations.literal: Only at the time internal governance was lax, knowledge of foreign conditions was cut off, and whether speaking of peace or war all failed to grasp the right moment—how could calamity have been escaped?
translations.idiomatic: Yet at the time domestic governance had grown lax, foreign realities were poorly understood, and advocates of peace and war alike misjudged the moment—how could disaster have been avoided?

sentences.zh: 鄧廷楨與則徐同心禦侮，克保岩疆。

translations.literal: Deng Tingzhen and Lin shared one heart in resisting insult and were able to secure the rocky frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Tingzhen worked in concert with Lin to resist foreign aggression and held the coastal frontier firm.

sentences.zh: 若達洪阿、姚瑩卻敵台灣，固由守禦有方，亦因敵非專注，朝廷皆不得已而罪之，諸人卒皆復起，而名節播宇內、煥史冊矣。

translations.literal: As for Da Hong'a and Yao Ying repelling the enemy in Taiwan, though this was indeed due to skillful defense, it was also because the enemy was not wholly focused; the court punished them all as a matter of necessity, yet in the end they all rose again, and their fame and integrity spread throughout the realm and shine in the historical record.
translations.idiomatic: Da Hong'a and Yao Ying likewise repelled the enemy in Taiwan—partly through sound defense, partly because Britain was not fully committed there. The court punished them all under pressure of circumstance, yet each was eventually restored to service, and their reputations spread across the empire and endure in history.
